title: Convex reduced objective: primitive gradients and function-value gap
summary: Solve the bilevel problem $\min_x\Phi(x)$, where $\Phi(x)=f(x,y^*(x))$ and $y^*(x)=\operatorname*{argmin}_y g(x,y)$ is the unique global lower-level solution. The upper- and lower-level variables are $x\in\mathbb{R}^{d_x}$ and $y\in\mathbb{R}^{d_y}$. Seek approximate stationarity of the reduced objective under the declared criterion and guarantee; assumptions on $f$, $g$, and $\Phi$ are specified separately.

task.detail: $\min_x\Phi(x)$, with a unique global lower-level minimizer
description_paragraphs: Solve the bilevel problem $\min_x\Phi(x)$, where $\Phi(x)=f(x,y^*(x))$ and $y^*(x)=\operatorname*{argmin}_y g(x,y)$ is the unique global lower-level solution. The upper- and lower-level variables are $x\in\mathbb{R}^{d_x}$ and $y\in\mathbb{R}^{d_y}$. Seek approximate stationarity of the reduced objective under the declared criterion and guarantee; assumptions on $f$, $g$, and $\Phi$ are specified separately.

regularity: The full population gradients of f and g are jointly L_f- and L_g-Lipschitz, respectively.
The blocks g_xy and g_yy are jointly rho_xy- and rho_yy-Lipschitz, respectively.
The bound $\|\nabla_yf(x,y)\|\le B_f$ holds for every $(x,y)$.
model.initialization: The points x0 and y0 are public, with ||y0-y*(x0)||<=R_y. Some x* minimizing Phi satisfies ||x0-x*||<=R_x.
model.other_geometry: The original $f$ need not be jointly convex; the convexity promise applies directly to $\Phi$.
description_paragraphs: The function $g(x,\cdot)$ is $\mu_y$-strongly convex on all of $\mathbb{R}^{d_y}$, uniformly for $x$. The quantities $\nabla f,\nabla g$ are jointly $L_f,L_g$-Lipschitz, and $g_{xy},g_{yy}$ are respectively $\rho_{xy},\rho_{yy}$-Lipschitz, in Euclidean induced operator norms.

The condition $\|\nabla_y f(x,y)\|\le B_f$ holds everywhere. The public initial point satisfies $\|y_0-y^*(x_0)\|\le R_y$, and there exists $x^*\in\arg\min\Phi$ satisfying $\|x_0-x^*\|\le R_x$. Joint convexity of the primitive $f$ is not assumed.

operations: The interface maps (h,x,y) to exact ∇h(x,y), choosing one h ∈ {f,g} per call.
oracle.auxiliary: Public-parameter arithmetic is free. Inner solutions, inverse Hessians, and hypergradients are not free.
description_paragraphs: All dimensions, model budgets, and initial points are public. At any $(x,y)\in\mathbb{R}^{d_x+d_y}$, the algorithm selects $h\in\{f,g\}$ and receives exact full gradient $\nabla h(x,y)$. One call returns only the selected function's gradient. The functions and lower-level optimum remain hidden.
No direct reduced-gradient, lower-level optimum, or inverse-Hessian interface is supplied. Arithmetic based on public data is free.
Return $\widehat{x}\in\mathbb{R}^{d_x}$, which may be an unqueried point or any admissible postprocessing of the transcript. An inner optimizer or certificate is not required.

resource.detail: Primitive cost: Q=N_f+N_g. Derivative resources (N_JVP,N_HVP) remain separate and are summed only under an explicit projection.
description_paragraphs: Each primitive gradient call costs one unit; $N=N_{\nabla f}+N_{\nabla g}$. The fixed worst-case budget includes every actual call used in initialization and inner computations.

Algorithms are deterministic and adaptive. Queries, stopping, and postprocessing may be arbitrary measurable functions of the transcript. The output may be unqueried, a deterministic selection of a past point, or an admissible average. No linear-span or zero-respecting restriction is imposed. Queries are sequential; each actual response in a parallel batch is charged separately. Arithmetic, linear algebra, and storage using received data are uncharged. Internal operations, memory, and communication are not tracked by this quantity.
There exists an algorithm determined by the public inputs such that $\Phi(\widehat{x})-\Phi^*\le\varepsilon$ holds on every admissible instance. The guarantee is deterministic and instancewise.

conditions: Tilde notation permits logarithmic factors in $1/\varepsilon$, with all structural budgets fixed. Every original gradient needed by a finite difference is charged separately.
applicability.dimension_conditions: The upper bound holds for every finite-dimensional instance in the declared model. Any dimension or fixed-budget dependence not displayed explicitly follows the accompanying evidence qualification.

bounds.hidden_constants: Unshown regularity, initialization, and noise budgets are fixed. Their joint parameter dependence is not certified as closed.
bounds.derivation:
Run the source algorithm at tolerance $\varepsilon/4$ for a fixed finite $K,N,M$ determined by public budgets. Bound finite-step error propagation recursively using public smoothness, distance, and gradient bounds, and allocate derivative-action errors so that the terminal-point perturbation is at most $\sqrt{\varepsilon/(8L_\Phi)}$. Convexity and $L_\Phi$-smoothness give $\|
abla\Phi(z)\|\le\sqrt{2L_\Phi(\Phi(z)-\Phi^*)}$, so the perturbed objective gap remains at most $\varepsilon$. Use the corresponding block of $[
abla g(x,y+hv)-
abla g(x,y)]/h$ for each action, with bias at most $ho|h|\|v\|^2/2$, choosing sufficiently small nonzero $h$ according to the current $\|v\|$. In the exact-real model without bit costs, smaller steps do not increase the number of primitive queries.

notes: The source permits blockwise smoothness constants. The joint constant $L_f,L_g$ bounds the relevant block constants, and $\|\nabla_yf\|\le B_f$ holds here. The displayed accuracy order fixes the other budgets; its leading parameter term is not asserted to remain uniform at zero endpoints.

Approximate each $g_{xy}v$ and $g_{yy}v$ by a deterministic finite difference of two exact gradients of the same function. The Hessian-block Lipschitz bound gives error at most $\rho |h|\|v\|^2/2$. Internal tolerances may be arbitrarily small at unchanged query cost. Allocate sufficiently small errors over the finite run to retain the target accuracy and asymptotic call count. Derivative-vector products are thereby simulated, not granted freely.
